Account.description: Registry entry. Never contains the credential.
Account.title: Account

AccountLease.description: What a leasing agent receives, including the credential to use.
AccountLease.title: AccountLease

AccountsSummary.description: Registry accounts behind an engine, by state. Counts only.
AccountsSummary.title: AccountsSummary

AdvancedOptions.description: Admin-only overrides on top of a template's defaults.
AdvancedOptions.title: AdvancedOptions

AgentRuntime.description:
What an agent says it runs, sent on heartbeat. Self-reported: it proves a
live process said so, not that the engine or model works.
AgentRuntime.title: AgentRuntime

AgentState.description:
Stored state. Whether an active agent is busy or idle is derived from the
tasks it holds, never stored, so it cannot drift.
AgentState.title: AgentState

AnswerOutcome.description:
One item's result: what was decided, not the whole decision (its question
is already known to the caller); get_decision reads it in full.
AnswerOutcome.title: AnswerOutcome

ArtifactRole.description: What an artifact is for, declared by its uploader (MCP operations 3.2).
ArtifactRole.title: ArtifactRole

ArtifactText.description: A byte range of an artifact, decoded as UTF-8 when it is text.
ArtifactText.title: ArtifactText

AwaitingQuotaRequest.description: An agent with no usable account asks for the work it cannot claim to wait.
AwaitingQuotaRequest.title: AwaitingQuotaRequest

BulkArchiveRequest.description:
Which terminal tasks to archive: all of `states`, narrowed by project and
by how long ago they last changed. `dry_run` only counts.
BulkArchiveRequest.title: BulkArchiveRequest

Check.description:
One measured fact about a pool's readiness. `ok` is None when it could not
be verified from here (`detail` says why); only False blocks a launch.
Check.title: Check

ClaimedTask.description:
A claimed task plus knowledge worth reading first: pinned pages, then the
best matches for the task in its project (references only).
ClaimedTask.title: ClaimedTask

ClaudeLogin.description:
A dedicated Claude login in progress. The link is shown only while
`pending`, only to the token that started it.
ClaudeLogin.title: ClaudeLogin

ClaudeLoginCode.description: The code the sign-in page shows. Sensitive: never echoed or logged.
ClaudeLoginCode.title: ClaudeLoginCode

CodexLogin.description:
A dedicated Codex login in progress. The code and link are shown only
while `pending`, only to the token that started it.
CodexLogin.title: CodexLogin

CostFigures.description:
What one group spent. `runs = measured_runs + not_reported_runs`. A token
field is null when no measured run carried it, never 0 (cost view 3.1).
CostFigures.title: CostFigures

CredentialUpdate.description: E.g. refreshed OAuth tokens for a subscription account.
CredentialUpdate.title: CredentialUpdate

Criteria.description: Deterministic acceptance checks for a local answer.
Criteria.title: Criteria

FactSource.description: How far a runtime fact is proven, weakest first.
FactSource.title: FactSource

Failover.description: The last switch of the account serving a task (account selection 3.6).
Failover.title: Failover

KnowledgeRef.description: A pointer delivered with a claim or a search: enough to decide whether to read.
KnowledgeRef.title: KnowledgeRef

KnowledgeWrite.description: Result of a create/edit: published directly, or proposed for review.
KnowledgeWrite.title: KnowledgeWrite

KubernetesOptions-Input.description: Where and how the `kubernetes` target runs an instance (one Pod each).
KubernetesOptions-Input.title: KubernetesOptions

KubernetesOptions-Output.description: Where and how the `kubernetes` target runs an instance (one Pod each).
KubernetesOptions-Output.title: KubernetesOptions

LeaseRequest.description:
Lease the best usable account globally (priority, then least leased).

The retired `providers` list is accepted and ignored: no caller-side order or
allowlist restricts selection.
LeaseRequest.title: LeaseRequest

LocalModelInfo.description: Measured from the server, never configured.
LocalModelInfo.title: LocalModelInfo

NanoclawOptions-Input.description:
The `nanoclaw` runtime (docs/research/2026-10-14.nanoclaw-integration).

NanoClaw bind-mounts paths from its own filesystem into agent containers, so
every path here is an absolute path **on the Docker host** and is mounted at
the identical path inside the NanoClaw host container.
NanoclawOptions-Input.title: NanoclawOptions

NanoclawOptions-Output.description:
The `nanoclaw` runtime (docs/research/2026-10-14.nanoclaw-integration).

NanoClaw bind-mounts paths from its own filesystem into agent containers, so
every path here is an absolute path **on the Docker host** and is mounted at
the identical path inside the NanoClaw host container.
NanoclawOptions-Output.title: NanoclawOptions

Page.description: A page with its current revision's content.
Page.title: Page

PoolPatch.description:
A partial pool update (MCP operations 3.3). Fields left out are kept; name,
target and runtime cannot change. `env` merges: a value sets a variable,
null removes it, and variables not named are kept (values are write-only).
PoolPatch.title: PoolPatch

ProgressKind.description: The closed set of structured progress milestones (progress-milestones spec 3.1).
ProgressKind.title: ProgressKind

QuotaReport.description:
One quota window as a provider stated it (account usage 3.1): a timed
window with a percentage, or a two-state pool (exhausted or not).
QuotaReport.title: QuotaReport

QuotaStatus.description: Whether Argus knows this account's quota, and if not, why (never a 0/100).
QuotaStatus.title: QuotaStatus

SaveToKnowledge.description: When answering a question: keep the answer as knowledge too.
SaveToKnowledge.title: SaveToKnowledge

Source.description: What justifies a revision: a task, decision, artifact, or URL.
Source.title: Source

TaskResult-Input.description: The one result envelope every task completes with (3.11).
TaskResult-Input.title: TaskResult

TaskResult-Output.description: The one result envelope every task completes with (3.11).
TaskResult-Output.title: TaskResult

Usage-Input.description: What the work cost, as reported by the agent. Recorded, never enforced.
Usage-Input.title: Usage

UsageReport.description: One engine run on one held account (account usage 3.2).
UsageReport.title: UsageReport

Verification.description:
Whether the stored bytes are the ones uploaded. Says nothing about whether
the content is acceptable.
Verification.title: Verification

argus_core__engines__Fact.description: One readiness fact: true, false, or unknown (None) with its evidence.
argus_core__engines__Fact.title: Fact

argus_core__engines__Readiness.description: Installed != authenticated != validated; usable only if all three hold.
argus_core__engines__Readiness.title: Readiness

argus_core__tasks__Usage.description: What the work cost, as reported by the agent. Recorded, never enforced.
argus_core__tasks__Usage.title: Usage

schema.title: Response List Accounts Api Accounts Get

post.description:
Register an account. A `credential` is written to the SOPS file first
(as `account-<id>`); the registry row only ever holds the reference.

The agent could not lease an account and so cannot claim: park the ready tasks
it could have taken as `awaiting_quota`. `409 account_available` if one is usable.

Start the official client's `setup-token` login for a new `anthropic`
account, or to renew `renew_account_id` (claude accounts spec 3).
Hand the sign-in page's code to the waiting client, once.

Start the official client's device-code login for a new `openai` account
(codex accounts spec 3). On success the account appears in the registry.

get.description:
Tokens and estimated cost per account, project and day over the window
ending now (cost view 3.3). Read only.

post.description:
Lease the best usable account globally (priority, then least leased), with
its credential. `runtime_providers` only states what the runtime can apply.
One active lease per role; it ends when released or replaced.
`409 no_account` when none is usable.
End the agent's leases: one `role`, or all of them.

get.description:
Reported tokens per account over [from, to), bucketed in the viewer's
timezone (account usage 3.5). Buckets with no rows are measured zeros.

delete.description:
Delete an account and, if nothing else references it, its Argus-generated
credential. `confirm_name` must equal the current name; `409 account_in_use`
while a lease is active.

SOPS and SQLite cannot commit together. The secret is removed inside the SQL
transaction, so a store failure rolls the rows back; if the commit then fails
after the secret is gone, the exact prior value is written back (compensation,
best effort: if that write also fails the error names the entry, never a value).

put.description:
Replace the credential (e.g. refreshed OAuth tokens). Allowed for the agent
holding a lease on the account, or an admin. If it cannot be persisted, the
account is disabled rather than left with a token that would be lost.

post.description:
Report that the leased account hit a quota. Returns the next account to use
(best remaining by priority, any provider), or none: then the given task is blocked as
`awaiting_quota` and returns to ready when an account frees up.

Read the provider's quota now (Codex only; account usage 3.3). At most once
per account per 5 minutes; never refreshes the credential.

Re-read the SOPS file after editing it by hand (`sops secrets.sops.yaml`),
then re-check every account's secret reference.

schema.title: Response List Admin Tokens Api Admin Tokens Get

post.description: Mint another admin token. The secret is shown only in this response.

schema.title: Response List Agents Api Agents Get

post.description: Mint a one-time token an agent redeems at registration.
Prove liveness and renew the listed task leases (each one independently).
Exit cleanly: the identity ends and its token is revoked.
Let the agent finish its current work, then claim nothing new.

get.description: The raw bytes. Honours `Range: bytes=…` for partial reads.

Up to `max_bytes` of a text or JSON artifact from `offset`, as UTF-8;
continue from `next_offset`. Other media types return `binary` and no bytes.

post.description:
Re-hash the stored bytes against the size and SHA-256 recorded at upload.
`ok` means intact, not acceptable.

get.description: Decisions oldest first, in pages (max 100); open ones by default.

post.description:
Answer up to 20 decisions, each with its own explicit answer and in its own
transaction. Each item succeeds or fails on its own (`ok`, `error`).

Answer an open decision. Approvals take `approve`/`reject`, reviews
`accept`/`reject` (with `text` as notes), questions their options or text.
With a `request_id`, a retry of the same answer by the same caller returns
the stored decision with `replayed: true` instead of 409 decision_not_open.

get.description:
Engines, executors and the local model: axes, auth methods and the three
readiness facts (installed, authenticated, validated). Read-only.

post.description:
One bounded completion on the local model, checked against `criteria`.
No tools act, so retrying or escalating duplicates no effect. An answer that
fails the criteria returns `verdict: escalate`; Argus does not start the
escalated work, the caller does.
Where should this task run? Deterministic; the decision is recorded.

A worker's channel switched its harness to follow a leased account
(codex accounts spec 3). Recorded for the audit trail; credentials never ride here.

get.description: Event history, newest first. Page backwards with `before`.

schema.title: Response List Events Api Events Get

get.description: Server-sent events. Reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` to resume without gaps.

Events after the cursor `after`, oldest first, waiting up to `wait_s`
seconds for one when none has happened yet (long-poll, like a claim). Without
`after`, waits for the next event from now. Keep `next_cursor` for the next
call; nothing is missed between calls.
What this node can run right now, measured from its targets (read-only).
Pool, queue, run-time, outcome and failure health over `window` hours.

The worker templates Argus supports, per node: ready, or exactly what is
missing. Read-only; nothing is created by looking.

post.description:
Create a pool from a template and request its first workers, in one
confirmed call. The pool is rebuilt server-side from the template; refusals
happen before anything is written. Success means *requested*.

get.description:
What waits on a manager, oldest first: blocked, in-review and
awaiting-approval tasks with their open decision, pending tasks stuck behind a
failed or cancelled dependency (`failed_dependencies`), plus open decisions
about pools and knowledge. `state` keeps only task rows in those states.

schema.title: Response List Instances Api Instances Get

get.description: The container's recent output, read live from the target (not stored).

post.description:
Replace a running instance without interrupting work: its agents drain, it
stops once none holds a claimed task, and a new one starts in its place.

Stop an instance now: its agents end immediately (tasks released); its slot
frees once the provider confirms the container is gone.

schema.title: Response List Pages Api Knowledge Pages Get

post.description:
Create a page. Workers may be limited to proposing (see
ARGUS_KNOWLEDGE_WORKER_WRITES); the response says which happened.
Confirm the page is still right; resets its freshness.

schema.title: Response List Revisions Api Knowledge Pages  Page Id  Revisions Get

post.description:
Publish an edit. `base_revision_id` must be the page's current revision,
otherwise `409 knowledge_conflict`: re-read the page and apply the change again.

get.description: Proposals are resolved by answering their `knowledge` decision.

schema.title: Response List Proposals Api Knowledge Proposals Get

get.description:
Full-text search over active pages (all words must match; if nothing does,
any word may). Stale pages rank after fresh ones.

schema.title: Response Search Api Knowledge Search Get

get.description: Prometheus text format; needs an admin token (`authorization` in the scrape config).
Fleet-wide totals per state for the Home view (orchestrator or admin).
Every pool; `env` shows its keys with redacted values.

schema.title: Response List Pools Api Pools Get

get.description: A pool; `env` values are redacted unless an admin asks for `reveal_env`.

patch.description:
Change some of a pool's options (admin only), keeping the rest. Requires
the `version` you read as `expected_version` (409 stale_version otherwise).
Name, target and runtime cannot change. `env` merges; null removes a key.

put.description:
Create or replace a pool definition, including its replica cap (admin only).
The reconciler converges instances to it within seconds. This replaces `env`
whole; PATCH changes single variables without resending the others.

get.description:
The pool, its live instances and agents, and per instance what is proven
about what runs there: each fact says its source (configured, requested,
started, validated) or `unknown`.

post.description:
Request one more worker from the pool. Refused (nothing changes) when the
node cannot start it now. Success means *requested*: the reconciler starts
the instance next pass; follow it in `/instances`.

Set desired replicas. Orchestrators may scale up to `max_replicas`; asking
for more opens a decision for a human (`decision_id`) instead of failing.

schema.title: Response List Projects Api Projects Get

get.description: Readiness plus the numbers /metrics reports, as JSON for the dashboard.

schema.title: Response List Kinds Api Task Kinds Get

put.description:
Create or replace a kind. Existing tasks keep the values they were created
with; schemas apply to new tasks and to results submitted from now on.

get.description:
Tasks newest first, in pages (max 100). `assignee` is the agent holding a
task now (claimed tasks only). `ids` (comma-separated, max 50) is a batch read
instead: no other filter, no paging, unknown ids in `missing`. Archived tasks
are left out unless `archived=true`, which lists only those.

post.description:
Orchestrators and admins create any task; workers only subtasks of a task
they hold. Past the per-agent hourly limit, an agent's new tasks wait for
human approval (a `policy` decision) instead of being refused.

Archive terminal tasks by state, project and age, answering how many.
`dry_run` counts without writing, for a confirmation. Non-terminal states
are refused (422 `state_not_archivable`) before anything changes.
Claim a ready task, long-polling up to `wait_s` seconds for one.

204.description: No matching task became ready within wait_s

post.description:
Archive a `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled` task; repeating it changes
nothing. Any other state answers 409 `task_not_terminal` and changes nothing.

get.description:
A task's artifacts (metadata only), by attempt then name; `in_result` says
whether the task's result lists one.

schema.title: Response List Artifacts Api Tasks  Task Id  Artifacts Get

post.description:
Upload the raw request body as an artifact of the attempt you hold.

List the returned id in `result.artifacts` when completing the task. `role`
says what it is for (report, delegate_report, …); it is never inferred.

Ask a question about the task you hold. The task is blocked until it is
answered; the answer is added to the task spec under "Clarifications" and
the task returns to ready.

put.description:
Replace the dependencies of a task that is still waiting (pending,
awaiting_approval or ready). A ready task with an unfinished new dependency
goes back to pending; a pending one whose dependencies all succeeded becomes
ready. Refuses cycles (422 dependency_cycle) and stale versions (409).

post.description:
Fail the attempt. A `provider_failure` that is a known quota notice of the
agent's engine account is not a failure: the account is exhausted, the task
returns to ready (or waits as `awaiting_quota`) and `failures` is unchanged.
Post a progress note (at most one per 10 s). Also renews the lease.
Return a `failed` task to `ready` with a fresh window of attempts (409 otherwise).
Return an archived task to listings and totals (admin). Idempotent.
